text:
For an **overnight pellet-smoker cook**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. Its 2,073.6Wh battery and 2,600W inverter give plenty of headroom for the startup igniter and, according to the cited estimate, about **two to three 12-hour cooks per charge**. A typical pellet grill uses much less power after ignition—roughly 35–60W—so the battery’s capacity matters more than a huge continuous wattage rating. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

For **one overnight cook**, a 1kWh-class station may be enough; the estimate is around 450–750Wh for 12 hours. Check your smoker’s startup draw and the station’s surge rating before buying, since the igniter can briefly pull substantially more power than the grill does once running. ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill))

At a campsite, keep the power station dry and well away from the grill’s heat, grease, and ash. And note: these estimates are for **pellet grills**, not electric smokers with heating elements, which need far more power.
